chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Abu Bakr al-Hazrami, who said:

I prayed the Maghrib prayer with my companions. So when I had prayed two rak'at, I gave the salam. So one of them said, 'You only prayed two rak'at, so repeat.' So I informed Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and he said: 'Perhaps you repeated?' I said, 'Yes.' He smiled, then said: 'It would have sufficed you if you had stood and prayed one rak'at.'

key_terms.سَلَّمْتُ: I gave the salam (concluded the prayer)

ai.seo_question: What should one do if they accidentally end their Maghrib prayer early by saying salam after two rak'at?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the principle of *takhfif* (ease) in prayer by distinguishing between a complete restart and a simple completion (*ibtida'*). Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) laughter highlights the practical wisdom of avoiding unnecessary burden, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence regarding *salat al-fard*. It establishes that for Maghrib, if one has already performed two rak'ats and then salam, the preferred correction is to stand and pray one more rak'at rather than repeating the entire prayer, reflecting the flexibility of the Imams in legal rulings.
